Subject: Performance SLO qualification — post-call recap

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the action items we discussed:

Summary of requirements (as I captured them)
- P95 latency target: 150ms for ~512-token responses (interactive search assistant).
- Sustained throughput: ~200 req/s across the fleet.
- Peak concurrency: ~50 concurrent sessions.
- Streaming: required for partial responses (user should see first tokens within 80–120ms).
- Target deployment region: US (primary), with later EU expansion.

Performance & cost constraints
- Need to balance latency SLO with cost — team asked for levers to hit SLO without 5–10x cost blowups.

Immediate next steps
1) You to share a small traffic sample (anonymized request/response sizes + percent streaming) and a recent tail-latency percentile from your current infra.
2) We’ll produce a short perf & cost note that maps levers (continuous batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles, model variants) to expected latency and unit cost.
3) If numbers look reasonable, schedule a 90-minute tech deep-dive + PoC plan (2–3 week PoC).

Attachments: SLO_matrix.xlsx (SLO breakdown), cost_model.csv (starter cost model).

Estimated timeline: I’ll aim to get the perf & cost note to you by Tue 2026-09-01.

Thanks — and happy to jump on a quick call if anything above is off.

Best,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification — post-call recap

Thanks for the clear recap — a couple of clarifying Qs I want before we do the costing:

1) Payload & token sizes: do they expect 512 tokens out only, or end-to-end (prompt + response) ~= 800–900 tokens? That changes KV cache behavior.
2) Streaming tolerance: they said streaming is required — need the percent of requests that will stream vs. non-stream. If 60–80% stream, it favors early-token-optimized paths.
3) Burstiness: is the 200 req/s fairly steady, or do they have 1–2 minute bursts that peak 2–3x? Batching strategy depends on burst profile.
4) Accuracy vs latency trade-offs: are there user-visible quality minima (e.g., specific evaluation metrics) where we must avoid distilled variants?

Quick notes on levers I’ll include in the perf note:
- Continuous batching (lower cost per-token when there’s headroom; still maintain p50/p95 targets via dynamic timeouts).
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (can reduce average compute by 20–60% depending on hit rate).
- Quantization profiles: int8 for parity-quality workloads; int4/mixed for aggressive cost targets (requires eval).
- Model variants: warm path = distilled 13B (low-latency, lower cost) + fallback to full 70B for edge cases; or use a 2-tier routing policy.

I’ll draft a back-of-envelope perf table and attach (perf_estimate.pdf) — will need the traffic sample to finalize.

-r

- Token sizes: average prompt + metadata ~= 300 tokens, expected response avg ~= 400 tokens (so end-to-end ~700).
- Streaming: ~70% of sessions will stream; initial tokens are high priority.
- Burstiness: steady baseline ~200 req/s with occasional marketing-driven spikes up to ~600 req/s for ~5–10 minute windows (we can absorb short degraded performance during spikes, but want graceful degradation).
- Quality constraints: we cannot use models that materially change phrasing for legal/brand reasons — any distilled variant must be validated against our eval set.

We can share a redacted traffic sample — I’ll drop it into the Drive folder by EOD today. Also can you provide a ballpark monthly spend estimate for the two approaches you mentioned (single large model optimized vs. 2-tier routing + quantization)? Need the numbers for procurement.
